# Change sets

`graph apply <file>` writes change set documents. One document is one
transaction: its operations apply in order and commit together or not at
all. Use it for batches and for new entities that link to each other; for
a single change the single-operation commands are simpler.

1. `graph whoami --json`: `max_batch` limits the operations per document.
2. Write the document to a file in the working directory (a harness may
   refuse other places): one JSON document, or JSONL with one document per
   line. Tell the user the file can be removed afterwards.
3. `graph apply <file> --dry-run --json`: checks everything and writes
   nothing. Read the findings and fix the document.
4. `graph apply <file> --json`. `data.results` has one entry per document;
   its `result.entities` lists every entity written with its `local` name,
   `id`, `alias` and new `rev` (`--summary`: only `entity_count`).
5. Read `data.results[].result.findings`; `graph get <id> --json` shows
   what was stored.

## Document

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ops` | no | The operations, 1 to 1000, applied in order. Needed unless `reconcile` is given. |
| `schema` | no | Always `graph_cli.changeset/1`. |
| `reason` | no | Why the change is made, for all ops. Needed when an op needs one (`supersede`, `retract`, or `require_reason` in `graph whoami`). |
| `idempotency_key` | no | Up to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`. Retrying the same document with the same key never writes twice. |
| `expect_seq` | no | Refuse unless the graph is still at this seq (`graph.seq` of the answer you read). |
| `source` | no | The source run the document comes from: `name` (lowercase, `a-z 0-9 _`), and optionally `version` and `run`. Recorded in the audit. Needed with `reconcile`. |
| `reconcile` | no | For pipelines that hand over the desired state of a source, not for agents: scopes with their items, applied by key in one transaction. |

## Operations

| Op | Required | Optional | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | `op`, `type` | `local`, `attrs`, `attrs_text`, `edges`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Create one entity, like `graph create`. `local` names it for later ops. |
| `update` | `op`, `id` | `set`, `set_text`, `unset`, `add`, `add_text`, `remove`, `remove_text`, `expect_rev` | Set, unset, add to or remove from attributes, like `graph update`. |
| `link` | `op`, `id`, `rel`, `target` | `qualifiers`, `target_rev`, `expect_rev` | Add an edge from `id` to `target`, like `graph link`. |
| `unlink` | `op`, `id` | `edge_id`, `rel`, `target`, `expect_rev` | Remove an edge by `edge_id`, or by `rel` and `target`. |
| `transition` | `op`, `id`, `to` | `attr`, `expect_rev` | Move the lifecycle of `id` to the state `to`. |
| `supersede` | `op`, `by`, `targets` |  | `by` replaces every entity in `targets`. |
| `retract` | `op`, `id` | `by`, `expect_rev` | Withdraw `id`; `by` names the entity that retracts it. |
| `set_alias` | `op`, `id`, `alias` |  | Rename the alias of `id`; the old alias still resolves. |

An edge in `edges` of a `create` has `rel`, `target` and optionally `qualifiers`, `target_rev`.

## Values

- An entity reference (`id`, `target`, `by`, `targets`) is a full id, an
  alias, or `@` and the `local` name of a `create` earlier in the same
  input (`@first`). Abbreviated ids are refused.
- `attrs` and `set` take typed JSON values; `attrs_text` and `set_text`
  take text converted by the attribute's datatype, as `--set` does. Name
  an attribute in only one of the two. A JSON number with a fraction is
  refused: write a decimal as a string or use the text form.
- A language-tagged field (base `lang_string` or `lang_text` in `graph
  describe fields`) holds `{"lang": "en", "value": "<value>"}`; its text
  form is `"<value>"@en` or `<value>@en`. A value without a tag is in the
  graph language (`graph graphs --json`); a graph without one refuses it.
- `add`, `add_text`, `remove` and `remove_text` take `{"<attr>": [...]}`
  for a list field: `add` appends each value not yet there, `remove` drops
  it; no read and no `expect_rev` needed. An attribute appears in only one
  of the update keys. An entity left as it was gets no new revision
  (`changed: false`, warning `entity.unchanged`); a document that changes
  nothing commits no transaction (`seq` null).
- `qualifiers` are typed JSON values on the edge itself (a page is a
  number); which ones a relation takes: `graph describe relations --json`.
  `target_rev` pins the revision of the target the edge refers to.
- `expect_rev` refuses the op unless that entity is at this revision, as
  `--expect` does.
- `valid_from` and `valid_to` take a date or an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- Names of attributes, qualifiers, states and `local` are lowercase:
  a letter, then letters, digits or `_`.

## Several documents

- JSONL: each line is its own transaction, in order. The whole input is
  parsed first, so broken input writes nothing. Processing stops at the
  first failing document; the documents before it stay written, and
  `data.results` shows which.
- `@` names bound in an earlier document stay usable in later ones.
- Give each document its own `idempotency_key`. `--idempotency-key` works
  only for input with a single document.

## Limits

- At most 1000 operations and 8 MiB per document, else
  `changeset.too_large`.
- A policy may set a lower `max_batch` per document, else
  `access.batch_too_large`. Then split the work into documents of at most
  `max_batch` operations (JSONL, in order) and tell the user that it is no
  longer one transaction.

## Reconcile documents

A pipeline (a scheduled job, a collector) hands over the desired state of a
source with `source` and `reconcile`; agents do not write these. `graph
apply` plans the difference by key under the graph lock and writes one
transaction: it creates what is new, updates what differs and leaves the
rest. `data.results[].result.reconcile` has, per scope, `created`,
`updated`, `unchanged`, `moved`, `adopted`, `kept`, `retired`, `revived`
and `retired_keys`.

| Scope key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | yes | The type of the entities the scope speaks for (its subtypes too). |
| `key` | yes | The attribute that holds the key: unique, one value, plain text. |
| `items` | yes | The desired entities, each with its `key`; may be empty. |
| `under` | no | Only the keys that start with this text belong to the scope; default all. |
| `complete` | no | True when the items are the whole scope: entities not listed are retired. Default false. |
| `fields` | no | The attributes the source sets; one an item leaves out is unset. |
| `edges` | no | The relations the source sets, outgoing edges only. |
| `retire` | no | `"retract"` (default) or `{"transition": "<state>"}` with optionally `attr` (the lifecycle attribute) and `"revive": "<state>"` for an item that returns. |
| `allow_retire` | no | Accept this many retires; needed above 5 and a tenth of the scope. |
| `allow_empty` | no | Accept a complete scope without items, which retires everything. |
| `keep` | no | Keys the source did not observe this run: left as they are. |
| `moves` | no | `{from, to}` gives the entity with the key `from` the key `to`; `{id, to}` gives a keyless entity its key. |
| `expect` | no | `min_items` and `max_items`: refuse a run whose item count lies outside. |

| Key in an item | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | yes | The item's key, within `under`; stored as `<source name>/<item key>`. |
| `type` | no | A concrete type of the scope's type; needed when that is abstract. |
| `local` | no | Names the entity for the edges of other items. |
| `attrs` | no | Typed values, only of attributes in `fields`. |
| `attrs_text` | no | The same as text, converted by the datatype. |
| `edges` | no | The desired edges: `rel` (one of the scope's `edges`), `target` and optionally `qualifiers`. |
| `valid_from` | no | Applies when the entity is created. |
| `valid_to` | no | Applies when the entity is created. |

- An item's key is stored as `<source name>/<item key>`, so a source only
  reaches its own entities.
- A scope is partial unless it is `complete`; only a complete scope
  retires. A retract is final (a key that comes back is a new entity); a
  `transition` keeps the entity and its key.
- Guards refuse the whole document and are audited, so a run that went
  wrong leaves the last good state: an empty complete scope
  (`reconcile.source_empty`, override `allow_empty`), more retires than 5
  or a tenth of the scope (`reconcile.retire_limit`, override
  `allow_retire`), an item count outside `expect` (`reconcile.shape`). A
  source that failed sends no entry for its scope.
- An edge target of an item is an id, an alias, an `@local`, or
  `{"type": "<type>", "attr": "<attr>", "value": "<value>"}`: the entity
  that holds that unique value, or the item of the document that will.
- At most 32 scopes, and 5000 operations after planning, the document's
  own `ops` included.

## Example

```json
{
  "schema": "graph_cli.changeset/1",
  "idempotency_key": "<value>",
  "reason": "<value>",
  "ops": [
    {"op": "create", "type": "<type>", "local": "first",
     "attrs_text": {"<attr>": "<value>"}},
    {"op": "create", "type": "<type>", "local": "second",
     "attrs_text": {"<attr>": "<value>"},
     "edges": [{"rel": "<relation>", "target": "@first"}]},
    {"op": "link", "id": "@second", "rel": "<relation>", "target": "<id>",
     "qualifiers": {"<attr>": "<value>"}},
    {"op": "update", "id": "<id>", "set_text": {"<attr>": "<value>"},
     "expect_rev": 3}
  ]
}
```
